content.comment_body: Hello, I would like to adjust the on and off times using the web interface. What steps do I need to follow to set this up?
I believe by 'web interface', you are referring to the [product_name] tool known as [product_name] web editor. To achieve what you want, you should utilize Parameter-VM-Mapping.
Yes, I did that. But in the [product_name] web editor, I still get a hexadecimal value displayed. I can change the hours but not the minutes. Ideally, I would like to set the time in an HH:MM format.

The hexadecimal format can be problematic. It's not possible to have both hours and minutes in a single input field; you need to create two separate fields, one for hours and one for minutes. I've attached an example for reference. To display values without the hex marker, check the discussion at [url].
When I try that, I end up seeing the hours twice, instead of separate inputs for hours and minutes.

It seems there might be an issue with your [product_name] configuration or your [product_name] web editor project. Without having your program and project files, it's difficult to provide a specific solution.

It's possible that the VM address for the timer is overlapping with another timer's VM address. When entering values in the web editor, the first two digits correspond to HH, and the last two represent MM. Each section occupies its own address. If you use a word-long VM address (for example, address no.1), it will use addresses no.1 and no.2 consecutively.
I downloaded the file and noticed the hexadecimal marker is still present; it has not been removed. Thank you and regards.
Which version of the [product_name] web editor are you using?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering challenges in configuring and displaying weekly timer switch times in an HH:MM format via the web editor. The default hexadecimal output is confusing, and separating input for hours and minutes is cumbersome. There are also mapping difficulties, including VM address overlap and questions on how to remove hex notation from the display, leading to user confusion and setup issues.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy-to-use web interface for setting weekly timer on/off times in a clear HH:MM format, enabling straightforward entry and display without hexadecimal values.
